segments.notes: 00:02.580–00:30.250 recaps synthesis then introduces analysis. Title only; no machine support. Analysis default is a chosen sampled square-wave bank, not an observed opening setup. Physical input indices run harmonic20 (index0) through harmonic1 (index19). Values are chosen normalized priors, never exact narration measurements. No per-part pose overrides. Freeze at first usable sample only; later motion cannot refit a setup. Independent inset footage may have different setups from the simultaneous whole-machine turntable: a single segment input cannot resolve that editorial mismatch.

00:02.580–00:38.980 describes twenty harmonics and asks how to set amplitude bars, without specifying opening values. analysis-01–09 contain actual whole-machine rotation/presenter and graph fade; rotations are camera changes, not mechanism setup changes. Preserve chosen prior; only bank offset may become identifiable from first usable geometry.
00:38.980–01:07.718 describes an even periodic square wave, twenty half-period samples used as inputs. analysis-10 is graphics only; hold prior, no geometric measurement or setup fit.

01:02.989–01:07.718 says sampled values are inputs; analysis-12 reason documents hand/measuring-stick bar setup and ten-high/ten-low annotation. Chosen normalized +/-0.4 sample prior uses harmonic/sample k*pi/20 and physical20..1 order, with jump endpoint chosen high to preserve the ten-high/ten-low pattern. Magnitude0.4 is conservative, not narrated displacement: actual built-magnifier/zero-fixture native renders accepted all80 integer bank positions at this scale. Full +/-1 was not justified by narration and exhausts the installed pen-wire branch at some crank positions. Requested observed bar fits can identify actual settings; continuous manual setting within the shot is only approximated by its first frozen frame.

01:11.600–01:25.809 crank produces coefficient-revealing function. 01:27.420–01:35.340 explicitly identifies physical high-left/low-right then edits to horizontal mirror; mirror is presentation, not amplitude order. 01:35.340–01:40.999 defines crank0; 01:52.419–02:18.299 describes every-second-turn sampling. analysis-14 pen/platen is first running view; bar and paired inset shots later cannot retroactively refit first-frame setup. Exact sample heights/phases/preload/feed gearing are chosen unless identified numerically. Keep crank fixed and fit only once; full bank period80, not one turn.

02:20.260–02:35.640 compares machine output to computer sinc, rescales twenty points and applies them to rocker bars. analysis-25 contains graph/sample graphics only; carry setup until real manual coefficient-setting view.

02:32.640–02:41.269 maps scaled measured sinc values to bars to produce square wave; analysis-27 reason documents actual measuring-stick adjustment. Choose even-square cosine coefficients with alternating odd-harmonic signs, normalized relative to fundamental: not a claim that the measured twenty coefficients equal the ideal Fourier series, nor that magnitudes are known. Numeric visible fits may adjust requested bars; nonobservable/dependent positions stay chosen. This continuously manipulated setup interval cannot be represented exactly by one frozen sample.

02:46.460–03:02.830 describes horizontal sections/drop/rise and cosine-only square synthesis. analysis-29 contains real moving pen/paper and camera pan; analysis-30 fades to drawing and analysis-31 is non-machine (hold). First usable pen/platen frame fixes requested observable output setup; full coefficient bank remains carried/chosen, never inferred from paper waveform alone. No later sample refits it.

03:04.340–03:31.390 summarizes Fourier analysis/synthesis and introduces next operation video. analysis-32–38 alternate whole presenter machine with diagram-only analysis-35. No documented physical reprogramming; carry frozen setup through graphic and fade intervals.
03:31.660–03:50.489 navigation narration. analysis-39–41 are blurred navigation thumbnails and credits through full video/audio end. Hold last mechanism setup; no fit or machine-validation claim.
